paras.text: The 9th Armored Division's Combat Command B finds the Ludendorff railroad bridge at Remagen standing on the afternoon of 7 March 1945 and crosses it; for ten days the Germans try to bring it down from the air, with artillery, with V-2s and with swimmers, and on the afternoon of 17 March it collapses. Told here from one record so far: Headquarters III Corps' after action report for March 1945 (its narrative, its G-2 report and its engineer journal). Hand-edited; every entry cites its PDF page in `ref`, with the printed page in its note. Fields as in `records/README.md` ("An engagement").

From 8 to 15 March the narrative gives, day by day, the raids on the bridge, the aircraft in them, and how many were "destroyed" (or "shot down") and "damaged". These are **the Corps' totals for all the antiaircraft units at the bridge together**: the narrative doesn't split them by battalion (only on 8 March does it name the battalions in the same paragraph, the 482nd AAA AW Bn and the 413th AAA Gun Bn). They are claims, not losses: they have not been checked against the Luftwaffe's loss returns, which are not online. From 11 March the report gives each day's period, 0600A to 0600A the next morning; before that it says only "during the day". The aircraft types are the US side's identifications (Stukas on 8 March, "ME-262s" on 14 March).

The report's times carry the letter A (UTC+1), as in "1550A". The engineer journal's entries (pdf 122) are typed without a letter ("171505 Mar"); they are taken as A, the report's own time, and say so.

The bridge is placed at the G-2 report's reference "F6520" (pdf 72), decoded on the Nord de Guerre grid (`tools/ndg_grid.py`): a four-figure reference names a 1 km square, and the point is its south-west corner; OpenStreetMap's bridge lies about 250 m north-east of it, inside the square. Remagen and Erpel are drawn at their centres (OpenStreetMap), and the heavy ponton bridge at the narrative's "wF673186" (pdf 38), decoded the same way.

The narrative's pages for 17-19 March are not in the scan (printed -41- onward; pdf 48 is a map and 49 a photograph), so 17 March here is the G-2 section's and the engineer journal's. Still to find: the 9th Armored Division's, CC B's, the 27th Armored Infantry Battalion's and the 14th Tank Battalion's own reports, and the antiaircraft battalions' and groups' reports (claims by unit), all in NARA RG 407 and not online; and the German side: the Luftwaffe's loss returns, the Wehrmachtbericht for these days, and the V-2 battery's firings. Nothing German is entered yet.

events.words: "The 9 Armd Div, having been given the mission of seizing REMAGEN and crossings over the AHR, moved out in the morning with CCA on the right and CCB on the left. ... CCB was to take REMAGEN and KRIPP (wF6718) and seize crossings over the AHR at SINZIG and BODENDORF (wF6317)."
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, narrative
events.note: Printed page -17-

events.placed: "By late afternoon"; no time typed in the narrative
events.words: "CCB met practically none and by late afternoon had captured REMAGEN, against light opposition."
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, narrative
events.note: Printed page -17-

events.placed: On the appearance of the US troops at the bridge; no time typed
events.words: "The bridge was thoroughly wired and mined with explosives for destruction, and on the appearance of our troops, an attempt was made to destroy it. But the demolition was only partially successful". The narrative: "only two small charges (or perhaps two detonators) were fired, and the bulk of the explosives failed to go off. Superficial damage was caused ... but structurally the bridge remained intact, although suitable for one way traffic only."
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, G-2 report and narrative
events.note: Printed pages -70- (G-2) and -17- (narrative, pdf 21). Both are the US side's account

events.placed: After the capture; the narrative types no time before "by midnight"
events.words: "Upon finding the bridge at REMAGEN intact, Lt Col Leonard Engaman [sic], CO 14 Tk Bn, who had received instructions from Brig Gen Hoge, CG CCB 9 Armd Div, to seize the bridge should the opportunity present itself, sent infantry and engineer elements of his task force to the east side of the river. ... One company was sent across the river initially, and by midnight the entire 27AIB, supported by tanks, had crossed."
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, narrative
events.note: Printed page -17-. The name is typed Engaman; it is usually spelled Engeman

events.words: "LUDENDORFF railroad bridge over the RHINE at REMAGEN (F6520) was captured intact at 1550A by alert troops of the 9th US Armored Division. ... According to prisoners of war, the bridge was to be blown at 1600".
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, G-2 report
events.note: Printed page -70-. The narrative gives no time of capture, only "by late afternoon" (pdf 21). The 1600 is what prisoners said, as the G-2 report gives it; no German record of the order has been found

events.words: "First news of the seizure of the bridge arrived at the Corps CP at approximately 1630A", by telephone from the 9 Armd Div's Chief of Staff to the Corps' Chief of Staff, who "instructed the 9 Armd Div to exploit the bridgehead as far as possible but to hold SINZIG." He then relayed it to Maj Gen Millikin.
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, narrative
events.note: Printed pages -17- and -18- (pdf 22). "Approximately" as typed

events.words: "The telephone call received at 2015A from First U S Army included information that the 7 Armd Div was attached to Corps immediately ... and that First U S Army was sending a 90mm gun battalion, a treadway bridge company and a DUKW company to Corps."
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, narrative
events.note: Printed page -18-

events.words: "RCT 47, having been motorized by Corps, became attached to CCB, 9 Armd Div, at 2100A".
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, narrative
events.note: Printed page -18-

events.placed: The day's total; no times typed
events.actor: AA units at the bridge (the Corps' total)
events.words: "the enemy attempted ten raids over the bridge with ten aircraft, eight of which were Stukas. By afternoon, however, the 482 AAA AW Bn (SP) had three batteries at the bridge site, with three platoons on the east and three platoons on the west bank of the river. The 413 AAA Gun Bn (90mm) went into positions on the west bank, and of the ten attacking aircraft eight were shot down."
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, narrative (8 March)
events.note: Printed page -22-. Claims, for all the AA units together; not checked against German losses

events.words: "Plans for AA defense of the bridgehead were begun during the night, and at about 0300A, 8 March, the 482 AAA AW Bn (SP) (atchd 9 Armd Div) was instructed to establish and maintain defense of the bridge with all available armament."
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, narrative
events.note: Printed page -19-. "At about" as typed

events.placed: The day's total; no times typed
events.actor: AA units at the bridge (the Corps' total)
events.words: "The enemy continued his air attacks on the bridge, making a total of eleven raids in which seventeen aircraft participated. Of these, twelve were destroyed and one damaged." The 16 AAA Gp "was directed to employ all AAA units for protection of the bridge": the 109 AAA Gun Bn on the west bank, the 634 AAA AW Bn (- Btry D) on the east.
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, narrative (9 March)
events.note: Printed page -25-. Claims, for all the AA units together; not checked against German losses

events.placed: The day's total; no times typed
events.actor: AA units at the bridge (the Corps' total)
events.words: "The enemy, during the day, made twenty one raids, in which he employed twenty eight planes. Of these nine were destroyed and one damaged." The 563 AAA AW Bn moved up, "to make a total of two gun and five automatic weapons battalions protecting these installations".
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, narrative (10 March)
events.note: Printed page -28-. Claims, for all the AA units together; not checked against German losses

events.placed: The period 110600 to 120600, as typed; no times within it
events.actor: AA units at the bridge (the Corps' total)
events.words: "During the period 110600 and 120600 the enemy made seven raids on the bridging sites, with thirteen aircraft. Five of these airplanes were shot down and two damaged." The 134 AAA Gun Bn (west of the river) and the 376 AAA AW Bn joined the defenses.
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, narrative (11 March)
events.note: Printed page -31-. Claims, for all the AA units together; not checked against German losses

events.words: "The heavy ponton bridge at wF673186 was ready for operation at 1700A, but was damaged by an LCVP which had gotten out of control, and it was 2400A before the bridge was opened."
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, narrative (11 March)
events.note: Printed page -31-

events.placed: The period 120600A to 130600A, as typed; no times within it
events.actor: AA units at the bridge (the Corps' total)
events.words: "During the period 120600A to 130600A the enemy greatly stepped up his efforts to destroy the bridges by aerial assault. A total of fifty eight raids were made by ninety one planes, twenty six of which were shot down and eight of which were damaged." At the close of the day: "sixteen 90mm batteries on the west bank; eleven and one half automatic weapons batteries on the west bank; and thirteen and one half automatic weapons batteries on the east bank."
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, narrative (12 March)
events.note: Printed page -33-. Claims, for all the AA units together; not checked against German losses

events.placed: The period 130600A to 140600A, as typed; no times within it
events.actor: AA units at the bridge (the Corps' total)
events.words: "The enemy again made a desperate bid to knock the Corps bridges out, when he sent ninety nine planes to make forty seven raids between 130600A and 140600A. Twenty six were destroyed and nine damaged."
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, narrative (13 March)
events.note: Claims, for all the AA units together; not checked against German losses

events.placed: The period 140600A to 150600A, as typed; no times within it
events.actor: AA units at the bridge (the Corps' total)
events.words: "he increased his effort to destroy the bridges by air attack and sent a total of ninety eight planes to make fifty seven raids between 140600A and 150600A. The majority of the planes on this day were identified as being ME-262s, jet propelled, and consequently only eight were destroyed and seven damaged. ... The AAA build up on this day reached its maximum strength -- a total of four gun battalions and nine automatic weapons battalions."
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, narrative (14 March)
events.note: Printed page -38-. Claims, for all the AA units together; not checked against German losses. "ME-262s" is the US side's identification

events.placed: The period 150600A to 160600A, as typed; no times within it
events.actor: AA units at the bridge (the Corps' total)
events.words: "Enemy air activity over the bridge decreased sharply, as only seven raids by twelve aircraft between 150600A and 160600A were reported. Of the twelve planes, two were destroyed and two damaged."
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, narrative (15 March)
events.note: Printed page -39-. Claims, for all the AA units together; not checked against German losses

events.words: "171030 Mar - Reports that enemy firing V-2's in attempt to destroy the bridge. Good progress being made on booms."
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, engineer journal
events.note: Printed page -116-. The journal types no zone letter; taken as A, the report's own time (assumed)

events.words: "171155 Mar - 1 Officer and 4 men killed and 33 men evacuated for wounds due to enemy V-2 (or some similar missile launched by the enemy)."
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, engineer journal
events.note: Printed page -116-. Zone taken as A (assumed). The journal doesn't say where they were hit or in which unit. The G-2 report (pdf 75): "on 17 March six V-2s fell on German soil, in the very general vicinity of the bridges. Our operations were not impeded, and no damage to the bridge resulted; however, one small German town was destroyed, and some US casualties resulted."

events.words: "the LUDENDORFF bridge, weakened by demolitions, artillery fire, near misses of bombs, and by heavy traffic, collapsed at 1500 March 17. It had served its purpose, and had been closed for repairs for several days; other bridges carried the traffic."
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, G-2 report
events.note: Printed page -73-. The time is typed without a zone letter; the report's A

events.words: "171505 Mar - Railway bridge collapsed. Cause undetermined. Check revealed two companies of the 276th Engr C Bn were working on the bridge at the time. As far as can be determined, approximately 90 casualties. ... At the time of the collapse, there was no enemy action in the area."
events.source: III Corps AAR, March 1945, engineer journal
events.note: Printed page -116-. Zone taken as A (assumed). The entry goes on to name two officers killed and to describe the collapse as witnesses gave it; left out here (the kit records units, not people)

claims.question: When was the bridge taken?
claims.note: The narrative gives no time for the bridge, only for Remagen's capture; the first word reached Corps at about 1630A

claims.question: When was the bridge to be blown?
claims.note: "According to prisoners of war": their statement as the G-2 report gives it, not a German record

claims.question: When did the bridge fall?
claims.note: Five minutes later than the G-2 report's round 1500; the journal types no zone letter

claims.question: Why did the bridge fall?
claims.answer: Weakened by demolitions, artillery fire, near misses of bombs, and heavy traffic

claims.question: Why did the bridge fall?
claims.answer: "Cause undetermined"; "no enemy action in the area" at the time
claims.note: The journal adds that several of the arch's tension members had been damaged, three severed, by artillery

claims.question: Did the V-2s of 17 March hurt anyone?
claims.answer: 1 officer and 4 men killed, 33 evacuated for wounds, at 1155
claims.note: "due to enemy V-2 (or some similar missile launched by the enemy)"

claims.question: Did the V-2s of 17 March hurt anyone?
claims.answer: Six V-2s fell; no damage to the bridge; "some US casualties"

claims.question: The AA claims, 8 March
claims.answer: 10 raids, 10 aircraft (8 of them Stukas); 8 shot down
claims.note: The Corps' total for all AA units (the 482 AAA AW Bn and 413 AAA Gun Bn are named); not checked against German losses

claims.question: The AA claims, 9 March
claims.note: The Corps' total for all AA units; not checked against German losses

claims.question: The AA claims, 10 March
claims.note: The Corps' total for all AA units; not checked against German losses

claims.question: The AA claims, 11 March (110600-120600)
claims.note: The Corps' total for all AA units; not checked against German losses

claims.question: The AA claims, 12 March (120600A-130600A)
claims.note: The Corps' total for all AA units; not checked against German losses

claims.question: The AA claims, 13 March (130600A-140600A)
claims.note: The Corps' total for all AA units; not checked against German losses

claims.question: The AA claims, 14 March (140600A-150600A)
claims.answer: 57 raids, 98 planes (the majority identified as ME-262s); 8 destroyed, 7 damaged
claims.note: The Corps' total for all AA units; not checked against German losses. The report puts the low count down to the jets

claims.question: The AA claims, 15 March (150600A-160600A)
claims.note: The Corps' total for all AA units; not checked against German losses

claims.question: The AA claims, 16-17 March
claims.source: III Corps AAR (the narrative's printed pages -41- onward are missing)
claims.note: The scanned narrative stops at printed -40- (pdf 47), in the 16 March entry; whatever it gave for 16 and 17 March is on the missing pages. pdf 47 not read for a total here

claims.question: How many raids in all?
claims.answer: "372 enemy aircraft made 223 raids in nine days on the bridge"
claims.note: The G-2 report's own total, for nine days; it doesn't say which nine, and it is not the sum of the narrative's daily figures above (8-15 March), which cover eight. Not added to them

positions.label: The Ludendorff railroad bridge (F6520)
positions.source: III Corps AAR, G-2 report, pdf 72 (printed -70-)
positions.note: The G-2 report's F6520, decoded on the Nord de Guerre grid (tools/ndg_grid.py F-650200): the south-west corner of the 1 km square the reference names. OpenStreetMap's Ludendorff-Brücke (50.5809 N 7.2445 E) lies about 250 m north-east of it, inside the square

positions.label: Remagen
positions.note: The town's centre. The narrative names the town without a grid reference

positions.label: Erpel
positions.note: The village's centre on the east bank at the bridge's far end

positions.label: The heavy ponton bridge (wF673186)
positions.note: The narrative's wF673186 decoded on the Nord de Guerre grid (tools/ndg_grid.py F-673186), to 100 m. Ready at 1700A on 11 March; opened 2400A
